The other day I was thinking of what kind of game I'd always come back to, and this one kept on coming to mind. Even though it does get a bit repetitive upon completion, the art style is so pretty and the music so relaxing that I can't help but just play it over and over. Potion Craft is a charming little simulator - there's a bit of a grind but it's not too difficult to figure your path to progression out, the puzzle aspect of understanding your customer's request is fun, and navigating through the paths and how to best utilize the ingredients is engaging.

One of my favorite aspects of Potion Craft is its artwork, and how unabashed it is on bringing cameos from other (popular or not as popular) from other games.

My only and biggest gripe with this game - and what has made me drop it entirely a year ago before I picked it back up again just recently - is that it's very unkind on your wrist/hand and is a bit of an acessibility nightmare. The only option you have is to make objects to be "Click to Pick Up" rather than having to hold the mouse down, but still you must do all the mashing on the mortar and mixing on the cauldron, which is quite punishing

I give it a solid 7.0 (Good) rating
Potion Craft excels most where it matters: the alchemical craft itself. The game absolutely nails the tactile joy of experimentation; charting new potion paths, refining techniques, and gradually building a library of perfected recipes gives a genuine sense of apprenticeship maturing into mastery.
In those moments, the game feels like a cozy place. You buy ingredients, you mull over how to improve your recipes, and you lose yourself in the quiet art of potion craft.

Outside that core loop, however, the experience thins; and unfortunately, very much so. The gardening, shopkeeping, and customer-request systems feel more like sketched frameworks than meaningful layers of strategy. They rarely push you to rethink your approach or engage with the alchemy mechanics in deeper, more varied ways. The haggling system, in particular, becomes tedious quickly; its
Once you unlock everything the game starts to lose its charm, but there's still a good bit of content that's enjoyable until that point.

Potion Craft has one of those mechanics that immediately feels different from almost anything else in the genre.
Instead of simply selecting ingredients from a recipe, you physically navigate around an alchemy map. Different ingredients, grinding levels, paths, bases, and combinations give you different ways of reaching the same effect, which creates a surprising amount of freedom despite how simple the basic system looks.
The shopkeeping side is much more straightforward, and overall I would say the game is fairly easy. Once you understand the mechanics and start accumulating money, the difficulty drops dramatically.
Visually, though, the game has a lot of personality. The manuscript-style artwork is distinctive, and the music and sound design make it an extremely relaxing game to play.
My biggest issue appeared after many hours: repetition.

Alchemist Simulator has got an excellent core gameplay loop for a game designed to let you dress up your potions and roleplay as an alchemist. Slowly decorate and build your magical cottage as you grow your herbs, brew your potions, and concoct mystic ingredients. Sell cure-alls, wonder-drugs, or vicious poisons. This game lets you fulfil the exact role a shut-in alchemist from Skyrim or WoW might live. 

No deadly enemies, just stubborn merchants trying to rip you off. Instead of grinding for drops, you're grinding up mushrooms to add to the cauldron. Tired of slaying bosses for a rare piece of loot? Try mixing dozens of ingredients to brew up the legendary Philosopher's Stone. It's a simple game, with simple mechanics, but the depths you will dive to create the most efficient potion will scratch an itch for satisfaction. I'd like to recommend this game, but I can't, the endgame is unfinished. There is no reason to make the philosopher’s stone (the ultimate goal of the game) because all you can use it for is making Life Salt & Philosopher’s Salt. However, Life Salt & Philosopher’s Salt are useless, by the time you are able to make them, you don’t need them. The gameplay is fun, but the non-ending is a huge letdown.

Cozy little management game where you put together potions. Ok, you don't put together, more like build a road with ingredients, as every ingredient can make a different intricate route. But good English is needed to understand what your customers want. Also, after a while, it's boring as you have to wait for the right merchant to progress, and the animation trailer is just a trailer; the game has a more puritan look. But all in all, I had my fun with it, but the endgame is so tedious and isn't worth it. In the end, you need to put together 12 very long routed potions. It is excruciatingly long and boring. I had been there from the beginning. Many updates have been done, and I've sunk many hours into the game. And where it stands, I still cannot recommend it. Especially since the end-game mechanics are still non-existent, plus some updates worsened things:

1) The watering mechanic adds literally NOTHING to the game but stretch gameplay hours out and increase the grind.
2) There is no reward for the grind. I've unlocked every talend and skill in the tree, but the game still sits at two gardens, one crystal cave, and one mushroom cave. All additional items are solely decorative.
3) Talking about the garden, fertilization is only possible once per day. No way to grind for seeds there with that talent, making you wait days and days to have one of the merchants provide more seeds for plants or crystals you actually need.

Changing recipes for the alchemy machine with an update is fine, I guess
